selected.hook_line: If bones were metal, would your body become stronger?
selected.viewer_expectation: A harder skeleton should make people stronger and safer.
selected.visible_contradiction: A metal frame holds weight well but cannot move like a living body.
selected.frame_zero: A small body model with metal rods bends less but loses its natural movement.
selected.character_action: The scholar gently bends two frame models to compare their responses.
selected.reaction: He pauses, surprised that strength alone does not solve the problem.
selected.activity: comparing flexible and rigid body structures
selected.topic_link: A material change can improve one feature while creating new limits.
selected.factual_anchor: Assume human bones were made of metal instead of the usual material.
selected.payoff: Metal bones might be strong, but a body would face problems with weight, movement and repair.
